newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: El Salvador probing origin of drug lord's Picasso.
newsitem.headline: El Salvador probing origin of drug lord's Picasso.

text.p: Police in El Salvador said on Friday they were investigating the authenticity of a painting attributed to Pablo Picasso that once belonged to late Colombian drug trafficker Pablo Escobar.
The painting, which depicts a couple embracing and is signed "Picasso," was confiscated from Salvadoran and Colombian drug traffickers when they were busted at a bar in San Salvador in May.

A police bulletin said its anti-narcotics division has asked the international police force Interpol for a report on the painting. "The painting could be a forgery according to the international experts Maurice Jardot and Laurants Quentin," the bulletin said.
Escobar's wife had bought the painting at an auction in Italy for $2 million as a birthday present for her husband, the police report said. The painting later disappeared from one of Escobar's homes.
Escobar was shot dead by a special army and police team in Medellin, Colombia, on Dec. 2, 1993.
